Running lab: `docker image inspect donhang-api:stage-1` -> linux/amd64; /etc/os-release in donhang-api -> Ubuntu 24.04.5 LTS; `dotnet --list-runtimes` -> Microsoft.AspNetCore.App 10.0.12.

claim_verdicts.evidence: api has no `ports:` (docker ps: donhang-api `8080/tcp`, unpublished); host curl to 172.28.0.13:8080 timed out. But Caddyfile also has `donhang.local:8443 { ... handle /api/v1/* { reverse_proxy api:8080 } }`, and `curl -k --resolve donhang.local:8443:127.0.0.1 https://donhang.local:8443/api/v1/products` -> 200. So the way in is Caddy on 8080 and 8443, not 8080 only.
claim_verdicts.source: examples/don-hang@stage-1: docker-compose.yml, Caddyfile; curl on running lab
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: The only way in is Caddy, which passes `/api/v1/*` requests on to the API; in this lesson you use its plain-HTTP port, `8080`.

issues.quote: The only way in is Caddy on port `8080`, which passes `/api/v1/*` requests on to the API.
issues.text: Not the only way in: the Caddyfile at stage-1 also proxies `/api/v1/*` to api:8080 on `donhang.local:8443`, and the running lab answers 200 there. The lesson's own point (only Caddy reaches the API) holds; the port is overstated.
issues.fix: Replace with: "The only way in is Caddy, which passes `/api/v1/*` requests on to the API; in this lesson you use its plain-HTTP port, `8080`."

issues.quote: Many programs connect to the database only when the first request needs it, so starting proves nothing about it.
issues.text: Key (c) is correct, but the explanation for (b) is wrong for the API the question names: DonHang.Api runs `context.Database.Migrate()` in Program.cs at startup, so it does reach its database before it starts serving. "Proves nothing" is false for this API.
issues.fix: Explanation b (en): "Some programs reach their database only on the first request; and even one that reaches it at startup can still answer nobody if users cannot reach its address." Update vi to match.
